label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.3 a.4…: In Aquinas' ST I q.3 a.4 first proof, each actually…
locator: I q.3 a.4 co., first proof: illud cuius esse est aliud ab essentia sua
interpretation: The direction is actual being with distinct esse/essence implies an actually existing cause of its esse that is another being, as a source inference from the explicitly stated causal dichotomy and no-self-causation principles. The literal reading is kept: 'habeat esse causatum ab alio' does not name the mode of causing, and the Lean type (CausesIn at esse) does not fix it. The efficient reading, suggested by the fire example and by the application to God 'quia Deum dicimus esse primam causam efficientem', is a separate statement that this claim only supports (#1633). The converse and the inverse claim that essence=esse excludes every external cause are not asserted. The application invokes God as first efficient cause; it does not define first cause by essence=esse or establish the two underlying premises outside Aquinas' argument.
attribution: The passage states 'oportet ergo quod illud cuius esse est aliud ab essentia sua, habeat esse causatum ab alio': whatever has esse other than its essence has its esse caused by another, which is the premise with the mode of causing left open. That the cause is actual and numerically other is the reading of 'ab alio' that the premise encodes; that it is efficient is not stated and is not part of the premise.
